_README: Every human judgement about the ROM lives in this file; the generated
listings are disposable. Locations are written 'space:$addr' -- 'f6:$4A92',
'b3:$8000', or 'rom:$F100' for an unbanked cart. Run tools/survey.py to see
Delete these _README keys or leave them; the tools ignore unknown keys.
_entries: Extra places to start tracing: jump-table targets, handlers the tracer cannot reach on its own. Add one whenever a JMP ($nnnn) or a computed jump leaves a hole.
_ram_vectors: Pairs of RAM addresses [low, high] holding a jump vector the hardware or the game calls through. The display-interrupt slot is the classic one. Without this, handlers reached only through a RAM vector never get traced and stay as .byte forever.
_bankat: Bank switches the tracer could not resolve, because the value written was not a tracked constant. Key is the location of the switch, value is the bank number it selects.
_labels: Names. Use them the moment you know what something is; renaming is free because regenerating is free.
_ram: Names for RAM addresses, keyed by hex address without a space prefix.
_headers: Block comments printed above a line. Good for explaining a routine's contract.
_blocks: Byte ranges to force as data rather than code, and to describe. Each entry takes 'loc' plus either 'end' or 'len', and may carry a 'note'.
A run that is data, not code. Add "gfx": true to draw each byte's bits
beside it instead of listing hex -- reading sprite data as a picture is
not the same work as reading it as numbers. "wide": true puts two bytes
on a line, which is what a 16-pixel 7800 sprite is.
_notes: Free-form notes attached to a space, printed in its listing header.
